properties.name: orientation
properties.comment: Which way the panels are laid out (Windows Forms' Orientation): vertical puts the splitter between a left and a right panel, horizontal between a top and a bottom one. A change re-derives the panel extents and the splitter cursor.
hand: written forgets the previous extents and updates the splitter cursor before invalidating the bounds

properties.name: splitter_distance
properties.comment: The first panel's extent along the orientation (Windows Forms' SplitterDistance). A read returns the effective distance after the panel limits; a write is the requested distance, kept and re-applied as the container resizes, and raises splitter_changed with SplitChangeReason::programmatic. A negative or non-finite value throws std::invalid_argument.
hand: a view: the write records the requested distance through set_distance; the read is the effective distance

properties.name: splitter_width
properties.comment: The splitter's visible thickness (Windows Forms' SplitterWidth), shorthand for splitter_geometry's visible_thickness that keeps the hit target centred. A zero, negative or non-finite value throws std::invalid_argument.
hand: a view onto splitter_geometry: the write derives a centred geometry and writes it

properties.name: splitter_hit_width
properties.comment: The least pointer target across the splitter, never below the visible thickness; shorthand for splitter_geometry's minimum_hit_target with the extra extent split evenly. A zero, negative or non-finite value throws std::invalid_argument.
hand: a view onto splitter_geometry: the write derives a centred geometry and writes it

properties.name: splitter_geometry
properties.comment: The seam's visible thickness, thickness policy and hit extents. The whole geometry is validated before any of it is published (std::invalid_argument for an invalid one); this is the form to use for asymmetric hit extents or a physical hairline, and splitter_width and splitter_hit_width are shorthands for it.
hand: written mirrors the visible thickness and hit target into splitter_width and splitter_hit_width before invalidating
properties.effects: Dirty::measure | Dirty::arrange | Dirty::paint | Dirty::hit_test | Dirty::semantics | Dirty::accessibility

properties.name: splitter_transition_duration
properties.comment: How long the seam's hot and pressed appearance takes to change; held by the splitter grip.
hand: a view onto the splitter grip's transition duration

properties.name: first_minimum
properties.comment: The least extent of the first panel (Windows Forms' Panel1MinSize, default 25). A negative, non-finite or above-maximum value throws std::invalid_argument and changes nothing.
prepare: require_finite_nonnegative(incoming, "first panel minimum must be finite and nonnegative");
throw std::invalid_argument("first panel minimum may not exceed its maximum");

properties.name: second_minimum
properties.comment: The least extent of the second panel (Windows Forms' Panel2MinSize, default 25). Refused as first_minimum is.
prepare: require_finite_nonnegative(incoming, "second panel minimum must be finite and nonnegative");
throw std::invalid_argument("second panel minimum may not exceed its maximum");

properties.name: first_maximum
properties.comment: The greatest extent of the first panel, or none for no limit. A negative, non-finite or below-minimum value throws std::invalid_argument and changes nothing.
prepare: require_finite_nonnegative(*incoming, "first panel maximum must be finite and nonnegative");
throw std::invalid_argument("first panel maximum may not be below its minimum");

properties.name: second_maximum
properties.comment: The greatest extent of the second panel, or none for no limit. Refused as first_maximum is.
prepare: require_finite_nonnegative(*incoming, "second panel maximum must be finite and nonnegative");
throw std::invalid_argument("second panel maximum may not be below its minimum");

properties.name: splitter_fixed
properties.comment: Whether the user may not move the splitter (Windows Forms' IsSplitterFixed). Programmatic distances still apply.

properties.name: fixed_panel
properties.comment: The panel that keeps its extent when the container resizes (Windows Forms' FixedPanel); none shares the change.

properties.name: collapse_panel
properties.comment: Optional seam-tab authority. Unlike fixed_panel, this identifies the pane toggled by a compact splitter tab and may remain operable while ordinary splitter resizing is fixed.
hand: written clears the automatic-collapse suppression and updates the grip's collapse appearance before invalidating

properties.name: automatic_collapse_threshold
properties.comment: Consumer-authored content threshold. Crossing below it automatically collapses collapse_panel; crossing back restores only an automatically collapsed pane. A user restore below the threshold is honored until the composition next crosses above it. Zero turns it off and restores an automatically collapsed pane. A negative or non-finite value throws std::invalid_argument.
hand: written clears the automatic-collapse suppression and, when turned off, restores an automatically collapsed pane before invalidating

properties.name: keyboard_increment
properties.comment: How far an arrow key moves the focused splitter (Windows Forms' SplitterIncrement, default 4). A zero, negative or non-finite value throws std::invalid_argument.
prepare: throw std::invalid_argument("splitter keyboard increment must be finite and positive");

not_properties.name: first_collapsed
not_properties.reason: set_first_collapsed takes the collapse origin as well; a method

not_properties.name: second_collapsed
not_properties.reason: set_second_collapsed takes the collapse origin as well; a method
